Note::reals¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::span<const double> Note::reals() const

Borrow The Float64 Lanes At Full Precision¶

reals() exposes a Float64 Note’s contiguous double lanes through a read-only span. It performs no allocation, conversion, rounding, or text formatting. This is the appropriate boundary when a numeric algorithm should consume continuous Note results without first building a std::vector<double>.

The span preserves the stored IEEE 754 values, including signed zero, infinities, and NaN payload bits. Printed representations may shorten decimal digits, but reals() accesses the original doubles. It never converts Int64 lanes even when their values would be exactly representable.

Shape And Lifetime¶

Lanes are presented in row-major logical order. Shape remains on the Note, so pass sizes_view() alongside reals() when an external operation needs both. A scalar has one lane and a defined empty Float64 Note has an empty span.

The span borrows memory. Keep the source Note or a storage-sharing Note view alive until the consumer finishes. host() is the owning alternative. Since the span element type is const, callers cannot mutate the Note through it.

reals() accepts only defined Float64 Notes. Use is_float64 before calling it when the dtype is dynamic.

Example 1: Consume Float64 Lanes Directly¶

const auto scores = pluss::note::make(std::vector<double>{0.25, 0.75});
const auto lanes = scores.reals();
std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lanes.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lanes[i];
std::cout << "] size=" << lanes.size() << '\n';

Output¶

[0.25, 0.75] size=2

Example 2: Higher-Rank Data Is Row-Major¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<double>{0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto lanes = grid.reals();
std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lanes.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lanes[i];
std::cout << "] shape=[" << grid.size(0) << ", " << grid.size(1) << "]\n";

Output¶

[0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5] shape=[2, 2]

Example 3: Empty Float64 Storage Is A Valid Empty Span¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<double>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{0});
std::cout << "empty lanes=" << empty.reals().size() << '\n';

Output¶

empty lanes=0

This differs from an undefined Note: the empty object has dtype Float64 and shape [0].

Example 4: Int64 Is Rejected Rather Than Converted¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).reals();
} catch (const pluss::Error& error) {
  const std::string message(error.what());
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

Note storage does not contain Float64 lanes

Example 5: Undefined Has No Floating-Point Buffer¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().reals();
} catch (const pluss::Error& error) {
  const std::string message(error.what());
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

Note::reals() on undefined Note
